task.title: Reset a user's one-time password in Keycloak
task.shortdesc: When a user loses or replaces the phone that holds their authenticator, delete its one-time password (OTP) credential. Then make the user set up a new one at their next sign-in.

ul.li: Confirm that the request comes from the user. Use a phone number or an address the user gave before they lost the phone, not one in the request.
Sign in to the admin console with an account that can manage the realm's users. I took the screens here as an administrator of the master realm.

context.p: For Keycloak administrators. Written for Keycloak 26.8.2 and checked against it. Every screen here comes from a Keycloak 26.8.2 server running on my own computer, with a test realm and test users. This is an independent guide, not official Keycloak documentation.

step.cmd: In the admin console, check that the user's realm is the current realm: its name is at the top of the menu. Select Users, search for the user, and select their username.

image.alt: The Users page, with the search box and the username alex.morgan marked

step.cmd: Select the Credentials tab. Find the row of type Otp. Its user label names the device, such as Alex's phone.

image.alt: The Credentials tab, with the Otp row of Alex's phone marked

step.cmd: Open the row's menu, and then select Delete.

image.alt: The row's menu open, with Delete marked

step.cmd: In Delete credentials?, select Delete. Keycloak reports The credentials has been deleted successfully., and only the password is left on the tab.

image.alt: The confirmation, with the Delete button marked

info.note: Don't stop after this step. Keycloak's default sign-in flow asks for a code only from a user who has a second factor set up. Without one, the user signs in with the password alone until step 5 is done.

step.cmd: Select the Details tab. In Required user actions, select Configure OTP, and then select Save. Keycloak reports The user has been saved.

image.alt: The Details tab, with Configure OTP in Required user actions and the Save button marked

step.cmd: Ask the user to sign in. After their password, Keycloak shows Mobile Authenticator Setup. They scan the code with an authenticator app on the new phone, type the code the app shows, name the device, and select Submit.

image.alt: Mobile Authenticator Setup, with the code, the device name and Submit marked, and the QR code hidden

result.p: On the Credentials tab, a new Otp row shows the name the user gave the new device, with today's date.

image.alt: The Credentials tab with the new Otp row, Alex's new phone, marked

result.p: Keycloak also keeps a record. When the realm saves admin events, Events > Admin events lists the deletion as an ACTION on the user's credential, and the new required action as an UPDATE of the user.

image.alt: Admin events, with the ACTION on the user's credential marked

ul.li: If Invalid authenticator code. appears during the setup, see When a Keycloak user can't sign in with a one-time password.
To see what the realm asks of an authenticator, such as the number of digits and how long a code lasts, see Keycloak OTP policy.
